shub.faq_env_1: TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET must be set in nodyx-core/.env. Create the app on dev.twitch.tv/console with the redirect URI https://<your-domain>/api/v1/streamer/twitch/callback.
shub.faq_env_2: STREAMER_OAUTH_KEY (32 hex bytes) protects the tokens in the database via AES-256-GCM + HKDF. node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
shub.faq_env_3: PUBLIC_BASE_URL must point to your public domain over HTTPS, it's the URL used for the EventSub webhooks (Twitch only delivers over HTTPS).
shub.faq_action_1: Sync EventSub: after a Nodyx update that adds new event types, or if a subscription appears failed.
shub.faq_action_2: Refresh tokens: only useful for debugging. The automatic refresh runs 30 min before expiration.
shub.faq_action_3: Disconnect: deletes the encrypted tokens. The EventSub subscriptions become orphaned on Twitch and will be recreated on the next connection.
shub.faq_trouble_1: "Pipeline failure" on callback: check TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, the Twitch redirect URL (exact match), and that PUBLIC_BASE_URL is over HTTPS.
shub.faq_trouble_2: Failed subscription: Twitch returned webhook_callback_verification_failed. Often an expired HTTPS certificate or a proxy blocking the POST with raw body. Reset the sub via "Sync".
shub.faq_trouble_3: No event after 30 min: the HMAC is probably invalid. Check the logs pm2 logs nodyx-core | grep EventSub.

cert.meta.title: Nodyx — CERT Detection Methodology
cert.meta.desc: Technical methodology used by the Nodyx honeypot system to generate qualified threat intelligence reports for CERT-FR and law enforcement.
cert.subtitle: Version 1.0 — Nodyx Security Honeypot — nodyx.org — AGPL-3.0
cert.tlp: TLP:WHITE — This document is public and may be freely redistributed.
cert.intro.p1: Nodyx is a self-hosted open source community platform (forum + chat + voice), released under the AGPL-3.0 license. Every Nodyx instance ships a passive honeypot system that captures, qualifies and documents intrusion attempts in real time.
cert.intro.p2: This document describes the methodology used to ensure that the reports sent to authorities (CERT-FR, ANSSI, hosting providers) represent qualified signal, not noise — so as to respect the time of response teams.
cert.trigger.p1: Botnets monitor domain-name creation feeds in real time via Certificate Transparency (CT) logs and new DNS zones. A domain like instance.nodyx.org typically receives its first scans within 10 minutes of creation.
cert.trigger.p2: This exposure window captures the latest versions of vulnerability scanners and active botnets — often before their signatures are integrated into global databases (AbuseIPDB, VirusTotal, Shodan). Each Nodyx instance therefore acts as an early-warning sensor for emerging threats.
cert.qualif.p1: An IP is only reported if it crosses at least one of the following criteria:
cert.trig.honeytoken.label: Honeytoken clicked
cert.trig.honeytoken.desc: The attacker clicked a trap link deliberately invisible to a legitimate user. Confirmation of a human actor.
cert.trig.canary.label: Canary file accessed
cert.trig.canary.desc: Access to a "decoy" file (fake .env, fake credentials.json) — clear intent to exfiltrate.
cert.trig.credential.label: Credential Harvest
cert.trig.credential.desc: Submission of credentials on a fake login form (wp-admin, phpmyadmin, panel…).
cert.trig.fingerprint.label: Recurring fingerprint
cert.trig.fingerprint.desc: Identical browser fingerprint (Canvas API) across several visits or several IPs — persistent attacker.
cert.trig.scan.label: Known vulnerability scan
cert.trig.scan.desc: User-Agent or network signature identifying a known tool: sqlmap, nuclei, nikto, Metasploit, Burp Suite…
cert.qualif.note: Plain 404 errors, legitimate SEO crawlers and known hosting-provider bots are filtered automatically. The targeted reporting rate aims for < 5 reports / day / instance.
cert.report.p1: Each report sent contains two attachments:
cert.report.md_desc: Human-readable by an analyst. Structured tables, full HTTP headers, browser fingerprint, legal qualification.
cert.report.json_desc: Ingestible by SIEM/SOAR. Versioned schema (1.0), typed fields, OWASP/CWE classification, MISP-ready integration.
cert.report.p2: Each report comes with a SHA-256 hash computed over the JSON, present in the mail body and in the SMTP header (X-Nodyx-SHA256). Evidence integrity is verifiable offline: sha256sum NODYX-CERT-*.json
cert.osint.p1: Before transmission, each IP is cross-referenced with three independent sources:
cert.osint.abuseipdb.desc: Abuse score 0–100, number of reports, attack categories
cert.osint.virustotal.desc: Analysis by 90+ AV/sandbox engines, global IP reputation
cert.osint.shodan.desc: Open ports, exposed CVEs, service banners (optional)
cert.osint.note: Results are cached for 24h (Redis) to preserve API quotas. The composite threat score (0–100) is included in each report.
cert.owasp.p1: The targeted HTTP path and the user-agent are analyzed to qualify the vulnerability being sought, enabling immediate classification in your tools:
cert.sovereign.p1: The CERT reporting module is entirely opt-in. Each instance's administrator controls, via their .env file:
cert.sovereign.note: Nodyx sends no data to central servers. No telemetry. No callback to nodyx.org. Each instance is sovereign and autonomous — that is the project's founding principle.

reputation.meta.title: How reputation works — Nodyx
reputation.meta.desc: A complete and transparent explanation of the Nodyx reputation system: Longevity, Quality, Engagement.
reputation.intro: Here, nothing is hidden. This is exactly how your reputation score is calculated — the formula, what it measures, and why it is designed this way.
reputation.philosophy: "Most social networks hide their algorithms because they optimize for your attention, not your contribution. Nodyx has no interest in manipulating you. This score is not here to grade you — it is here to show you your journey."
reputation.global.title: The global score
reputation.global.p1: The percentage shown at the center of the rings is the simple average of the three dimensions below:
reputation.global.p2: Each dimension is independent and capped at 100%. A global score of 100% takes time, consistency, and involvement — not optimization.
reputation.longevity.title: Longevity
reputation.longevity.p1: Measures how long you have been part of this community. A member present for one year has 100% longevity.
reputation.longevity.note: This dimension cannot be sped up. It simply rewards loyalty over time.
reputation.quality.title: Quality
reputation.quality.p1: Measures the real relevance of your contributions via the Thanks received, weighted by a time-decay coefficient. A recent Thanks weighs more than an old one.
reputation.quality.formula_aria: Q = (sum of Thanks received / sum of total Posts) × Weight(λ)
reputation.lambda.title: The Weight(λ) coefficient — time decay
reputation.lambda.p1: Each Thanks received is weighted by its date. The older a Thanks, the less it weighs. The decay follows an exponential law:
reputation.lambda.li_t: t = time elapsed since the Thanks, in days
reputation.lambda.li_lambda: λ = decay coefficient — configurable by the instance administrator
reputation.lambda.li_high: high λ → old Thanks count very little (short memory)
reputation.lambda.li_low: λ close to 0 → all Thanks weigh the same (long memory)
reputation.merci_note: The Thanks system is being rolled out. In the meantime, Quality is approximated by accumulated XP points (min(1, XP ÷ 500)). As soon as the Thanks data is available, the full formula will take effect automatically.
reputation.engagement.title: Engagement
reputation.engagement.p1: Measures whether you start discussions or merely reply. Creating threads is valued twice as much.
reputation.engagement.note: The goal is not to create threads for the sake of it — but to value those who enrich the community by opening up spaces for discussion.
reputation.gaming.title: Can this score be gamed?
reputation.gaming.p1: Not really. Longevity is strictly time-based — you can't speed up time. Quality requires real investment over the long run. Engagement can be "optimized" by creating empty threads, but the community notices and those threads have no real value.
reputation.gaming.p2: Besides, this score is not a ranking. There is no hidden reward for reaching 100%. It is simply an honest reflection of your journey here.
reputation.evolution.title: This system will evolve
reputation.evolution.p1: In time, other dimensions may be added by each instance's administrators (helping other members, event participation, moderation…). Every change will be documented here. The formulas will always remain public and readable.
reputation.footer: Nodyx is open-source under the AGPL-3.0 license. The code that computes this score is readable by anyone on GitHub.

e2ebackup.restorebox.text: You have a backup. On another device, or if your encrypted messages don't show here, restore your key.
e2ebackup.btn.restore_here: Restore my key on this device
e2ebackup.note.legacy_key: Your key was created before this feature: it cannot be backed up yet. Prepare a compatible key in one click, with no risk to your future messages.
e2ebackup.warn.regen: A new key will replace the old one. Old encrypted messages already shown on this device will no longer be decryptable here. Your new messages, however, will be protected and backed up.
e2ebackup.examples: Examples that work well: sun-tiger-piano-melon-lighthouse · my old cat sleeps on the piano
e2ebackup.hint.tip: Tip: 4-5 random words, or a short sentence that only means something to you. The longer it is, the stronger it is. If you lose it, the backup stays tamper-proof but can no longer be opened, so write it down carefully.
